facts.text: Generative models are machine-learning systems that create new, realistic-looking images or sensor data; "generated weather" uses these systems to add rain, fog, snow, dust or night to clear-weather recordings.
facts.quote: Generative models are machine-learning systems that create new, realistic-looking images or sensor data, and "generated weather" means using them to add rain, fog, snow, dust or night to a recording made in clear weather.

facts.text: Generative weather editing can turn thousands of hours of clear-weather recordings into bad-weather data without waiting for winter.
facts.quote: thousands of hours of clear-weather recordings could become "bad weather" data without waiting for winter.

facts.text: Generated weather edits are valid for some testing, but are not yet a substitute for physically traceable sensor simulation.

facts.text: A 2026 benchmark found that a panel of vision-language models accepted the best generative editor's weather and lighting edits as realistic 94.8% of the time, compared with 26.3% for the best rule-based library.

facts.text: Physics-informed generators that incorporate range, material reflectance and scattering are stronger than aesthetic filters for generating weather edits.

facts.text: A survey of 91 studies characterizes the generative weather field as early-stage.

facts.text: No standard or regulator treats generated weather as physically equivalent to real sensor measurements.

facts.text: A photorealistic generated image can be wrong in absolute brightness, depth, glare energy, raindrop paths and consistency between the camera and the lidar or radar observing the same scene.
facts.quote: A photorealistic image can be wrong in exactly the quantities that matter: absolute brightness, depth, glare energy, raindrop paths, and consistency between the camera and the lidar or radar looking at the same scene [Chapter 6].

facts.text: Generated rain, fog or dust should carry a physical label such as "20 mm/h rain" or "50 m visibility" only when the label has been calibrated against real sensor data; otherwise, the generated weather is a domain perturbation whose exact physical meaning is unknown.
